column1: # The six FP scaling/prototype probes, executed on master.  Each was built with
# the original `scripts/build-opt.sh` at -O2 into its own ROOT, then run serially
# under a named 8 GiB scope with a 1800 s cap.  Raw output, argv, wall and peak
# RSS per run are under generated/master_port/fp/probe_runs/ (UNTRACKED:
# /generated/ is gitignored); the build command and build time are in each
# ROOT's build.cmd / build.time.
# BINARIES (sha256)
#   s2a_probe    4fc4a3fca37f67a933605adb5edff56996b1c596f9fe7ddd7eae205e078f9541
#   s2_probe     6117ddc87632a1a5765aa3360c0c398b6265fb7e91f42b0f1f2cca7bacc8f12a
#   s3_probe     6ffd3408fa497a6fcc636d74f0eeffb71703365f9b0e2b835e241a623e4aab94
#   s1_identity  dc293ae90f10d68be018c27e5a157937c881a1932e46ad94f6f72977aeff246b
#   perf_probe   0243aceb7353addfbdc0d5833a196f20ec04d97c8e1fb5bbbf23356627c8c3b8
# CERTIFICATE
#   instr_scan_gate.dcert, sha256 41533d1c315437991614088efbfabc325e3daf1a128c2d62fcc27485c5aa20aa
#   1235 sources, 1264 nodes, 0 flops, all six SupportedByProjection fields true
# WHAT THESE PROBES CANNOT DO ON ONE BUILD.  S1/S2/S3 are specified as "ONE
# source, built TWICE" -- once against a tree whose proved specializer is S1's
# (0f175676b) and once against the current tree.  In all three probes
# `specS1 = Projection.mixDriver`, i.e. whatever the CURRENT tree's proved
# specializer is, so the label `s1`/`host` is BUILD-RELATIVE, not a pinned
# implementation.  Master's five specializer files are byte-identical to the S3
# pin, so on this build every `s1`/`host` column is the SAME code.  The
# cross-build S1-vs-S2 comparison is therefore NOT executed here and is not
# credited.  `PartialEvaluatorSummary.lean` and `PartialEvaluatorShift.lean` do
# not exist at 0f175676b at all.
# Consequence: s2_probe and s2a_probe are the SAME experiment on one build.
# Their sources differ only in prose, labels, the backend keyword (host vs s1)
# and one extra printed field (s2 prints the HOST digest); both compare
# `mixDriver` against `ProtoSum.mixDriver`.
# `identical` / `same` in a grid line is `digest A == digest B`: a 64-bit
# structural hash over the whole residual term (constructor tag, literals, var
# indices, primitive codes, ctor names, case alternatives, call targets).  Equal
# digests are strong evidence of an identical residual, NOT a proof of it.

column1: # CROSS-PROBE CONSISTENCY (independent binaries, independent builds)
#   s2-grid vs s3-grid, HOST column: the 25 lines cover 20 DISTINCT (S, N, E)
#     coordinates (S=256,N=256,E=512 recurs in sweeps A, B, C and D); all 20
#     agree on both term count and digest, 0 disagreements.
#   s0-grid (fork) vs s2-grid (host): 15 genuinely shared coordinates, all agree
#     on term count.  The 2 apparent mismatches are coordinate collisions, not
#     disagreements: s2's `dyn` sweep reuses (S=64,N=64,E=128) and
#     (S=256,N=64,E=128) with every source dynamic, which is a different design.
#   instr_scan: `mixDriver`, `ProtoSum.mixDriver` and `ProtoShift.mixDriver`
#     all produce 48439 terms, checker bound 5711 and digest
#     16712272993486204376, and the earlier total_probe row-15 record agrees
#   No probe log in this set contains the string `false`, nor FAILED, REJECTED,
#   OUT OF FUEL or NOT SupportedByProjection.
# perf_probe's RSS COLUMN IS NOT A PEAK AND IS NOT USED.  Measured: in one
# process it reports 9104, 9116, 9136 then 8408 kB -- it goes DOWN.  Sampling
# /proc/<pid>/status from outside the same run shows the same non-monotonicity
# (max VmHWM observed 9176 kB, final 8408 kB, /usr/bin/time %M 8412 kB), so the
# column tracks residency at print time rather than a high-water mark and is not
# comparable with %M.  The mechanism was not pinned down.  The figure of record
# for every row above is the guarded runner's %M in peak_rss_kb; no claim here
# rests on the probe's own column.
